findings.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin calls IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(String) and a six-argument constructor (loaded, cacheKey, realm, searchKey, cached, parentQuery) that do not exist on the existing IdentityProviderListQuery class in this module. The module fails to compile: the existing IdentityProviderListQuery exposes only the single-set accessor and the (revision, cacheKey, realm, idps) constructor, so both the multi-org-keyed lookup (getIDPs(orgId)) and the merge-with-previous-query constructor invoked on the cache-miss-after-invalidate path are unresolvable symbols.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the wrong alias literal: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) registers a cleanup for a non-existent IDP named "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, and this same wrong literal is repeated for the idp-alias-20 creation at the later step. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns null, so the method-reference creation throws a NullPointerException immediately when testCacheIDPForLogin runs, failing the test before any caching assertions execute; additionally the actually-created IDPs are never registered for cleanup.

[ADVISORY] The two cache-write paths in getForLogin use inconsistent revision arguments: the fresh-miss path passes startupRevision to addRevisioned while the search-key-miss path after invalidateObject passes cache.getCurrentCounter(). Whoever maintains cross-node invalidation semantics gets bitten: mixing the session's startup revision with a freshly-read counter means the second write can be accepted on a node where the revision no longer matches the invalidation epoch, reintroducing a stale query entry that getForLogin then serves; the test only asserts entry existence, not which revision was stored.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally performs a delegate getByAlias lookup (idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)) before checking the cache, adding a storage round-trip on every removal even when the cached path previously avoided it. Operators running high-churn IDP deletion against a slow custom IdentityProviderStorageProvider get an extra uncached delegate read per remove() that the previous code only paid on the isInvalid branch.

[BUG] The test's cleanup registration fetches the wrong alias: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` instead of `"idp-alias-" + i`, so none of the 20 created IDPs are ever removed. At teardown, `get("alias")` resolves a resource for a non-existent provider and remove() throws 404 during cleanup (failing unrelated subsequent tests in the realm), and even if it didn't, all 20 `idp-alias-*` brokers leak into TEST_REALM_NAME for the rest of the suite, corrupting IDP counts in later cache tests.

[BUG] The second cleanup registration repeats the wrong-alias bug: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` for the `idp-alias-20` provider. The `idp-alias-20` broker created in step 1 leaks into the realm after the test (and the cleanup lambda targets a non-existent `"alias"` provider), so subsequent tests in the same realm see a stale keycloak-oidc broker with BROKER_PUBLIC set.

[ADVISORY] The merge branch of getForLogin (query != null but getIDPs(searchKey) == null, i.e. a second organizationId / empty search cached into an existing list query) has no test coverage — the new test only exercises one organizationId per FetchMode, so the invalidateObject/re-merge path with the 6-arg IdentityProviderListQuery constructor is never executed. A regression in the merge constructor (e.g. dropped old searchKeys, or the inconsistent revision argument `cache.getCurrentCounter()` vs `startupRevision` in the first branch) would ship unverified; anyone caching a second org's login IDPs in a cluster gets stale or missing IDP lists with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] remove() of a login-eligible IDP (which must invalidate the login caches via registerIDPLoginInvalidation) is never verified — the test only removes a disabled, non-login IDP (idp-alias-1) and asserts caches survive. If registerIDPLoginInvalidation is skipped or mis-predicated on the remove path (e.g. storedIdp being null for an already-removed alias making the Objects::nonNull predicate false), deleted brokers would keep appearing on login pages served from cache, and no test would catch it.

[ADVISORY] The newly added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check for wrapped IDPs in both branches of searchForIdentityProviders has no test in this diff, and the test that exercises getForLogin caching never asserts that a disabled IDP is filtered from the rendered login page when served from the cache path. If the caching layer ever serves a disabled IDP model (the exact scenario the re-check guards against), a login page would render a dead broker button; the mitigation line could be deleted in a refactor with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate SPI change (excluding org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC) alters behavior for every storage provider implementation, including the non-cached default, but no dedicated unit test of the predicate itself exists in this diff — only indirect coverage via cache counts. A subtle predicate change (e.g. treating org-linked public IDPs as excluded for REALM_ONLY, or NPE when getConfig() returns null for an org-linked model built by a third-party provider) would silently change which brokers appear on login for all implementations, verified only by fragile count assertions in one cache test.

[BUG] This PR adds a semantic change to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (filtering out org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs) that alters getForLogin behavior for every storage implementation, including the non-cached JPA/Map providers, and is not traceable to the stated 'add caching for getForLogin' requirement. All consumers of getLoginPredicate — including uncached IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations and any other caller (e.g. admin console listings, other filters built on this predicate) — silently change behavior when this PR merges: org-linked non-public IDPs disappear from results even when caching is disabled; if BROKER_PUBLIC filtering is actually needed only for the cache's invalidation logic, it belongs in the cache layer, not the SPI default predicate.

[BUG] The test cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) registers a null resource whose remove call throws NPE/ResourceNotFound during cleanup. testCacheIDPForLogin leaks the 20 created IDPs (and org links) into the test realm for every subsequent test in the class, breaking test isolation and causing unrelated tests in OrganizationCacheTest to see phantom identity providers; if Resource#get on an unknown alias throws instead of returning null, the cleanup itself fails the test suite.

[ADVISORY] The re-added `idp.isEnabled()` filter, commented as needed because 'idp might have been wrapped', is a symptom patch for the cache provider's createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper dropping/garbling the enabled flag, smuggled into a PR whose stated scope is caching. Any future caller of getForLogin that does not independently re-check isEnabled() (e.g. new login pages or API endpoints) will render disabled IDPs as clickable login options whenever the org-aware wrapper is in play; the invariant 'getForLogin only returns enabled IDPs' is enforced by post-filtering at one call site instead of in the wrapper or the cache provider, which is the next change that gets riskier because of this.

[BUG] getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-"+i, so the lookup returns null and the method-reference receiver is evaluated eagerly, throwing a NullPointerException immediately when addCleanup is called. The new test testCacheIDPForLogin fails with an NPE at provider-creation time, so none of the caching behavior it purports to verify is actually exercised; the same copy-paste bug recurs after creating "idp-alias-20".

[BUG] The cache-hit path in getForLogin builds the result from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the cache-miss path and the null-idp fallback path do apply it, so the same logical call returns differently-wrapped models depending on whether the list cache was warm. Organization-aware login pages get raw IdentityProviderModel instances on cache hits but wrapped ones on misses; any behavior the wrapper adds (e.g., hiding the IDP from non-org contexts or altering its displayed alias/config) silently differs between requests, and the re-check of isEnabled() in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean hints the wrapper already changes semantics that this path loses.

[ADVISORY] The merge branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) while the initial-population branch uses startupRevision, an inconsistency with the revision-ownership pattern the surrounding cache code uses. If getCurrentCounter() is lower than the startup revision used by other invalidations, the merged query can be stored under a stale revision and be resurrected after an invalidation that should have evicted it, serving stale login IDP lists across nodes.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (storedIdp) even when the alias cache entry is valid and could supply the invalidation data, adding a delegate DB round-trip to every IDP removal. Administrators removing IDPs in bulk (or cleanup paths removing many brokers) pay one extra storage hit per removal that the pre-diff code only paid on the invalid-cache branch; a hot admin path regresses from cached to uncached.

[ADVISORY] The new organization-visibility filter is baked into the shared getLoginPredicate(), changing getForLogin results for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA map storage, cache, custom SPI providers) rather than being a property of the login-page consumer. Any third-party storage provider or caller that relied on getLoginPredicate (e.g., other LoginFilter consumers listing brokers for login) now silently excludes organization-linked non-public brokers; the semantic change ships without a contract note or versioning, so out-of-tree implementers of the SPI see behavior shift beneath them.

[ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate() change bundles a functional behavior change (org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are now excluded from login results) into a PR whose stated intent is only caching, silently changing the semantics of every getForLogin caller including non-cached storage providers. Users of realms where an org-linked broker was previously shown on the login page (because the old predicate had no org/BROKER_PUBLIC clause) lose that IDP from the login selector after this deploy, with no mention of the behavioral change in the PR objective; this is intent drift from 'add caching' to 'also change login IDP visibility'.

[ADVISORY] The cache key cacheKeyForLogin omits organizationId, so each distinct organizationId for the same FetchMode evicts the previously cached searchKey: the query!=null branch calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and rebuilds, discarding the other organization's cached result set. Realms with multiple organizations (the core use case of ALL/ORG_ONLY fetch modes) thrash the shared cache entry per organization, degrading to repeated delegate round-trips; in a cluster, concurrent requests for different orgs repeatedly invalidate each other's entries.

[ADVISORY] The new-query-in-existing-entry path uses cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision for addRevisioned while the initial-population path uses getCurrentRevision(cacheKey) and startupRevision, so the second organization's write can register a revision that conflicts with the invalidation-revision scheme used elsewhere in RealmCacheManager. A later invalidation registered with a revision derived from the standard scheme may not evict the entry created with getCurrentCounter(), leaving stale login IDP lists served after an update to an IDP linked to a second organization.

[ADVISORY] The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check filters out OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrappers whose isEnabled() reflects the organization's enabled state, changing which IDPs render on the org login page — a behavioral change to the login UI smuggled into a caching PR. When an IDP is linked to an organization that is disabled, the IDP disappears from the login selector where it previously appeared; if the wrapper's isEnabled() delegates to the org (as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel does), this alters login UX for org members with no explicit requirement that the org's enabled state gate the member-facing selector.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` for every created IDP, which returns null for all 21 created providers and throws NullPointerException during method-scoped cleanup. The test fails (or aborts) in its cleanup phase and, more importantly, none of the 20+ created IDPs are actually registered for removal, corrupting the test realm for other tests in the class if cleanup ordering masks the NPE.

[BUG] The test's cleanup registers removal of an IDP with the literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20 created IDPs are never cleaned up. The cleanup resource targets a nonexistent alias, producing a 404/NPE at cleanup time and leaving 20 broker IDPs (plus idp-alias-20) in the test realm, which breaks other tests in the realm and makes the test's own cache assumptions unreliable across reruns.

[BUG] The cleanup for idp-alias-20 also uses the literal alias "alias" (getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)) instead of "idp-alias-20". Same failure mode as the loop cleanup: the second-created IDP is never removed, and the dangling cleanup resource hits a nonexistent alias, so any assertion about realm state after this test is polluted.

[ADVISORY] The test verifies only the cache's internal IdentityProviderListQuery contents (getIDPs sizes); it never asserts the Stream returned by getForLogin() itself in any scenario. The most important behavior — what callers actually receive — is unverified. Notably, the cached path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin returns models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping applied on the isInvalid path, so cached and uncached calls can return differently-shaped models; a content assertion on the returned stream would catch this, but the test passes either way because it never looks at the return value. Checked files: OrganizationCacheTest.java is the only test file in this diff touching getForLogin.

[ADVISORY] The new branch where a cache entry exists but getIDPs(searchKey) returns null (query present, new organizationId search) has no test triggering it — the test only ever calls getForLogin with the same organizationId (or null) used to populate the cache, and asserts counts, never the invalidateObject/re-add path with a second organization. The multi-organization merge path — invalidateObject, re-fetch, and the new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, ..., query) constructor that must carry over the previously cached search keys — is entirely unexercised; a regression that drops the prior searchKey's IDP set (e.g. showing an empty login page for the first org after a second org logs in) passes the suite. Checked files: only OrganizationCacheTest.java touches this provider, and it never calls getForLogin with a second, distinct organizationId.

[ADVISORY] The stale-entry fallback branch (session.identityProviders().getById(id) == null → registerInvalidation and re-fetch from delegate) is never triggered by any test. This is the cache-poisoning recovery path — a cached IDP list referencing a since-deleted IDP (e.g. deleted by another node or a path that bypassed invalidation). If this branch has a bug (wrong key invalidated, or the delegate re-fetch also wrong), users get an empty or erroring login page permanently, and no test in the diff would notice. Checked files: OrganizationCacheTest.java never creates the condition of a cached list containing a nonexistent internalId.

[BUG] update() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) and that method dereferences original (original.getOrganizationId()) without a null check, so updating an IDP whose getById lookup returns null throws NullPointerException before the delegate update runs. Any update() where the underlying provider returns null for the internalId (e.g. custom IDP storage where cached lookup misses and delegate returns null, or stale internalId passed by a caller) crashes with NPE instead of updating, leaving the IDP unmodifiable and the login caches un-invalidated.

[ADVISORY] When a cache entry exists but lacks the current organizationId searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) locally and then re-reads getCurrentRevision and replaces the query, so the invalidation is not propagated to other cluster nodes the way registerInvalidation-based invalidations are, while the new query is only addRevisioned on this node's current counter. In a multi-node cluster, node A caches the org-scoped list while node B retains the previous query object lacking that searchKey (or vice versa after revision races), so subsequent getForLogin calls on other nodes take the invalidate-and-replace path repeatedly, degrading to per-request cache misses or serving a query whose revision predates a concurrent update — stale login IDP lists shown on the login page.

[ADVISORY] When a cached internalId no longer resolves (getById returns null), the code registers invalidation of only the single cacheKey for the current (realm, mode) and falls back to the delegate, leaving the other FetchMode caches for the same realm populated with the same stale id set. After an IDP is removed in a way that bypassed this provider's invalidation hooks (e.g. direct persistence-layer delete or another node's race), every FetchMode cache (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) holds the dangling id; each mode's first access falls into the same fallback, and between invalidation and re-population users on the login page can be served lists from the still-stale sibling-mode caches.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate arm `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, unlike the existing filter chain which may tolerate config-less models. Any IdentityProviderModel returned by a custom storage or legacy data where getConfig() returns null now throws NPE from getLoginPredicate during every login-page IDP listing and during every create/update/remove through the Infinispan cache provider, breaking login flows for that realm until the row is fixed.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and never applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cache hits and cache misses return differently-shaped IdentityProviderModel objects. The cache-miss/isInvalid branches wrap every delegate result with this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (organization-aware enable/disable semantics), but the cached branch returns raw models from getById. A user hitting the login page after the list query is cached gets unwrapped models, producing different visibility/enablement behavior than the first, uncached request — the exact class of bug the freemarker isEnabled re-check in this same diff papers over, meaning the cached path can list IDPs on the login page that the uncached path would have hidden.

[BUG] The new predicate clause dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, so any IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set but a null config map throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate. getLoginPredicate().test(idp) is now invoked from InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/remove/update invalidation paths (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), so creating or updating an organization-linked IDP whose config map is null (models constructed programmatically or by storage providers that leave config unset) throws NPE and aborts the admin write operation instead of just skipping cache invalidation.

[ADVISORY] remove(String alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a delegate/DB hit) even on the branch where isInvalid(cacheKey) is true and the result is only used for invalidation bookkeeping. Every IDP removal in a realm using the infinispan cache pays an extra storage lookup on the hot admin path even when the login-cache invalidation it feeds will be a no-op for a non-login IDP; operators of large realms see doubled read load on IDP removal with no correctness benefit when the IDP does not qualify for login.

[ADVISORY] The getForLogin cache stores per-organizationId sets inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode and, on a miss for a new searchKey, invalidates the whole object and re-adds with cache.getCurrentCounter(), a different revision basis than the startupRevision used on the first populate. When addRevisioned in the second branch fails because the revision/counter basis is not newer than the entry concurrently re-populated by another node (the two populate paths use inconsistent revision sources: startupRevision vs getCurrentCounter), the freshly loaded set for the new organizationId is silently discarded — every login-page request for that organization keeps missing the cache and re-hits the delegate storage, turning the login cache into a permanent passthrough for that org with no error or metric surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin` implementation, the two cache-population paths do pass different revision values to `cache.addRevisioned(...)`: on a cold miss (`query == null`) it uses `startupRevision`, while on a “searchKey not cached” path (`cached == null` after `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`) it calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then uses `cache.getCurrentCounter()`. This inconsistency is clearly present in the diff and is a concrete review concern because revision/counter choice affects cache/invalidation semantics, but the diff alone does not let us verify the claimed cross-node stale reintroduction behavior (depends on `addRevisioned`/revision semantics not shown).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check, and then uses `storedIdp` for `registerIDPInvalidation(...)` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. Previously, the delegate lookup happened only in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch (`registerIDPInvalidation(idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias))`), while the cached branch could avoid a storage read by using the cached entry. This is a diff-grounded performance/extra round-trip concern rather than a functional defect.

The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only ever calls `getForLogin` with one `organizationId` value per `FetchMode` (REALM_ONLY with null/"", ORG_ONLY with `orgaId`, ALL with `orgaId`), so it never triggers the “second searchKey” merge path. adjudication.rationale: The new remove() logic now calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` (after prefetching `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin()` only removes `idp-alias-1`, which is created as disabled (`setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`), so it is not login-eligible and the test asserts login caches remain. There is no test case that removes a login-eligible IDP (one that satisfies `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`) and then asserts the login caches (keys from `cacheKeyForLogin(...)`) are invalidated/cleared, so regressions in the remove-path invalidation predicate would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new safeguard in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)` to re-check `idp.isEnabled()` because the IDP "might have been wrapped" (both branches now do `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))`). The only new test, `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` caching and asserts cached set sizes, but it never goes through `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` nor asserts that a disabled IDP would be filtered at the login-page bean level specifically in the cached/wrapped-model scenario that motivated the re-check. So the finding that this new mitigation lacks a targeted regression test is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate SPI change (excluding org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC) alters behavior for every storage provider implementation, including the non-cached default, but no dedicated unit test of the predicate itself exists in this diff — only indirect coverage via cache counts. A subtle predicate change (e.g. treating org-linked public IDPs as excluded for REALM_ONLY, or NPE when getConfig() returns null for an org-linked model built by a third-party provider) would silently change which brokers appear on login for all implementations, verified only by fragile count assertions in one cache test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SPI-wide behavior in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding an extra constraint for org-linked IDPs: `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. That predicate is used by all `IdentityProviderStorageProvider` implementations, not just the Infinispan cached one. The only new test added here (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercises `getForLogin()` and cache invalidation/counts, but it does not directly assert the predicate’s edge cases/contract independent of caching (e.g., org-linked + missing/false `BROKER_PUBLIC` behavior). The NPE risk mentioned (null `getConfig()`) is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This PR adds a semantic change to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (filtering out org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs) that alters getForLogin behavior for every storage implementation, including the non-cached JPA/Map providers, and is not traceable to the stated 'add caching for getForLogin' requirement. All consumers of getLoginPredicate — including uncached IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations and any other caller (e.g. admin console listings, other filters built on this predicate) — silently change behavior when this PR merges: org-linked non-public IDPs disappear from results even when caching is disabled; if BROKER_PUBLIC filtering is actually needed only for the cache's invalidation logic, it belongs in the cache layer, not the SPI default predicate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* introduce a semantic change in the shared SPI-level `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` (in `server-spi/.../IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`). That predicate is then used from the cache layer (`InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` imports `getLoginPredicate` and uses it to decide whether to invalidate login caches). Because the predicate lives in the shared SPI, any other caller or storage implementation that relies on `getLoginPredicate()` (including non-cached providers) would see behavior change, which is a legitimate scope/architecture concern. However, the diff also adds functional usage consistent with the new semantics (e.g., `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` calls `getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null)` specifically to fetch “public enabled IDPs linked to any org”, and the tests configure `BROKER_PUBLIC` for org-linked IDPs), so it’s not clearly a defect introduced by the PR—rather, a potentially broader-than-stated change that should be explicitly justified/documented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) registers a null resource whose remove call throws NPE/ResourceNotFound during cleanup. testCacheIDPForLogin leaks the 20 created IDPs (and org links) into the test realm for every subsequent test in the class, breaking test isolation and causing unrelated tests in OrganizationCacheTest to see phantom identity providers; if Resource#get on an unknown alias throws instead of returning null, the cleanup itself fails the test suite.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, inside the loop creating IDPs with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup hook is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal string "alias"). This does not correspond to any of the created IDPs and therefore will not remove them during cleanup. As a result, the test will leak created identity providers into subsequent tests, and depending on `identityProviders().get("alias")` behavior, the cleanup registration/invocation can also fail (e.g., null or missing resource). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The re-added `idp.isEnabled()` filter, commented as needed because 'idp might have been wrapped', is a symptom patch for the cache provider's createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper dropping/garbling the enabled flag, smuggled into a PR whose stated scope is caching. Any future caller of getForLogin that does not independently re-check isEnabled() (e.g. new login pages or API endpoints) will render disabled IDPs as clickable login options whenever the org-aware wrapper is in play; the invariant 'getForLogin only returns enabled IDPs' is enforced by post-filtering at one call site instead of in the wrapper or the cache provider, which is the next change that gets riskier because of this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` adding `idp.isEnabled()` as a defensive filter with a comment about wrapping. However, the finding’s core claim—that `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` “drops/garbles the enabled flag” and therefore disabled IDPs could be returned/clickable—is not verifiable from this diff: the wrapper’s implementation is not shown, and `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` relies on `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` for the actual filtering, only mapping to `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` on the cache-miss path. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that disabled IDPs are returned by `getForLogin` or that the wrapper changes `isEnabled()` semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-"+i, so the lookup returns null and the method-reference receiver is evaluated eagerly, throwing a NullPointerException immediately when addCleanup is called. The new test testCacheIDPForLogin fails with an NPE at provider-creation time, so none of the caching behavior it purports to verify is actually exercised; the same copy-paste bug recurs after creating "idp-alias-20".

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup registration uses `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal `"alias"`). Since no IDP with alias `"alias"` is created in this test, `identityProviders().get("alias")` will return null, and the instance method reference `null::remove` requires evaluating the receiver immediately, causing an NPE at cleanup registration time. The same incorrect cleanup line is repeated after creating `idp-alias-20`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path in getForLogin builds the result from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the cache-miss path and the null-idp fallback path do apply it, so the same logical call returns differently-wrapped models depending on whether the list cache was warm. Organization-aware login pages get raw IdentityProviderModel instances on cache hits but wrapped ones on misses; any behavior the wrapper adds (e.g., hiding the IDP from non-org contexts or altering its displayed alias/config) silently differs between requests, and the re-check of isEnabled() in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean hints the wrapper already changes semantics that this path loses.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path rebuilds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. The null-idp fallback also applies the wrapper. This makes the returned `IdentityProviderModel` instances differ depending on whether the list cache is warm, which is a correctness/behavior inconsistency introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The merge branch calls cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) while the initial-population branch uses startupRevision, an inconsistency with the revision-ownership pattern the surrounding cache code uses. If getCurrentCounter() is lower than the startup revision used by other invalidations, the merged query can be stored under a stale revision and be resurrected after an invalidation that should have evicted it, serving stale login IDP lists across nodes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably introduces inconsistent revisioning for the same cache entry key in `getForLogin(...)`: initial population uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “merge/add searchKey” path invalidates and then stores with `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded. However, the finding’s claim about cross-node resurrection/stale revision behavior depends on unseen cache/revision semantics (what `startupRevision` and `getCurrentCounter()` guarantee), so a concrete correctness defect can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (storedIdp) even when the alias cache entry is valid and could supply the invalidation data, adding a delegate DB round-trip to every IDP removal. Administrators removing IDPs in bulk (or cleanup paths removing many brokers) pay one extra storage hit per removal that the pre-diff code only paid on the invalid-cache branch; a hot admin path regresses from cached to uncached.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` (so it runs on every removal). Previously, the delegate lookup by alias was only performed in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch (`registerIDPInvalidation(idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias))`), while the valid-cache branch used the cached entry to obtain invalidation data. This is a concrete, diff-grounded potential performance regression (extra delegate/storage hit per removal), not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new organization-visibility filter is baked into the shared getLoginPredicate(), changing getForLogin results for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA map storage, cache, custom SPI providers) rather than being a property of the login-page consumer. Any third-party storage provider or caller that relied on getLoginPredicate (e.g., other LoginFilter consumers listing brokers for login) now silently excludes organization-linked non-public brokers; the semantic change ships without a contract note or versioning, so out-of-tree implementers of the SPI see behavior shift beneath them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavioral/contract change to the shared SPI-level predicate: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now additionally filters out organization-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true (`.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`). Because `getLoginPredicate()` is a shared utility in the SPI, this change can affect any caller/provider that uses it (not just the new Infinispan cache logic), which matches the finding’s concern about cross-implementation semantics shifting without being localized to the login-page consumer. The diff does not prove it’s incorrect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/compatibility concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getLoginPredicate() change bundles a functional behavior change (org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC are now excluded from login results) into a PR whose stated intent is only caching, silently changing the semantics of every getForLogin caller including non-cached storage providers. Users of realms where an org-linked broker was previously shown on the login page (because the old predicate had no org/BROKER_PUBLIC clause) lose that IDP from the login selector after this deploy, with no mention of the behavioral change in the PR objective; this is intent drift from 'add caching' to 'also change login IDP visibility'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a functional/semantic change in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will exclude org-linked IDPs from `getForLogin(...)` unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true. This affects every `getForLogin` caller and every storage provider using that predicate, not just the new Infinispan caching layer. Whether that is intended can’t be proven from the diff alone, but the finding’s core point (behavior change beyond caching) is directly grounded in the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache key cacheKeyForLogin omits organizationId, so each distinct organizationId for the same FetchMode evicts the previously cached searchKey: the query!=null branch calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and rebuilds, discarding the other organization's cached result set. Realms with multiple organizations (the core use case of ALL/ORG_ONLY fetch modes) thrash the shared cache entry per organization, degrading to repeated delegate round-trips; in a cluster, concurrent requests for different orgs repeatedly invalidate each other's entries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` intentionally does not include `organizationId`, but the cached value (`IdentityProviderListQuery`) is keyed internally by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or "") via `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`. When a new `searchKey` is requested and missing, the code rebuilds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` passing the prior `query`, which indicates it is designed to *retain* previously cached per-organization result sets within the same cache entry rather than evicting them. Therefore the claim that each distinct `organizationId` “evicts the previously cached searchKey” is not supported by what’s shown in the diff (at worst, there’s an extra invalidate/rewrite step, but not the described discard/thrash behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new-query-in-existing-entry path uses cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision for addRevisioned while the initial-population path uses getCurrentRevision(cacheKey) and startupRevision, so the second organization's write can register a revision that conflicts with the invalidation-revision scheme used elsewhere in RealmCacheManager. A later invalidation registered with a revision derived from the standard scheme may not evict the entry created with getCurrentCounter(), leaving stale login IDP lists served after an update to an IDP linked to a second organization.

adjudication.rationale: In the new caching logic for getForLogin(), the initial population path stores a revisioned entry via `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)` after capturing `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)`, while the “existing entry but new searchKey” path rebuilds the query and calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and could plausibly interact poorly with whatever revision/invalidation scheme `RealmCacheManager` expects, but the diff alone does not show the semantics of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, `getCurrentRevision`, or `getCurrentCounter`, so the claimed stale-cache behavior cannot be conclusively verified from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check filters out OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrappers whose isEnabled() reflects the organization's enabled state, changing which IDPs render on the org login page — a behavioral change to the login UI smuggled into a caching PR. When an IDP is linked to an organization that is disabled, the IDP disappears from the login selector where it previously appeared; if the wrapper's isEnabled() delegates to the org (as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel does), this alters login UX for org members with no explicit requirement that the org's enabled state gate the member-facing selector.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an additional UI-side filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)` by changing `.filter(idp -> !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` to `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))`. Since `getForLogin(...)` in the Infinispan provider now returns wrapped models (`.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`), this extra `isEnabled()` check can change which IDPs render depending on how the wrapper implements `isEnabled()`. However, the specific claim that `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel.isEnabled()` “reflects the organization's enabled state” (and thus hides IDPs when an org is disabled) is not shown in this diff, so that part can’t be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration uses `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` for every created IDP, which returns null for all 21 created providers and throws NullPointerException during method-scoped cleanup. The test fails (or aborts) in its cleanup phase and, more importantly, none of the 20+ created IDPs are actually registered for removal, corrupting the test realm for other tests in the class if cleanup ordering masks the NPE.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i` (and later `"idp-alias-20"`), the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal string "alias"). This does not target the created providers, so they are not properly removed during cleanup and may pollute the realm / affect subsequent tests. The finding’s specific claim about `get("alias")` returning null and causing an NPE isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (it could instead fail with a not-found on remove), but the cleanup bug itself is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test's cleanup registers removal of an IDP with the literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20 created IDPs are never cleaned up. The cleanup resource targets a nonexistent alias, producing a 404/NPE at cleanup time and leaving 20 broker IDPs (plus idp-alias-20) in the test realm, which breaks other tests in the realm and makes the test's own cache assumptions unreliable across reruns.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the loop creating IDPs with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i` registers cleanup via `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal string "alias"), which does not match the created aliases. The same incorrect cleanup registration appears after creating `idp-alias-20`. This means the created IDPs will not be removed by cleanup (and cleanup may fail against a nonexistent alias), leaving test state behind and potentially breaking subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup for idp-alias-20 also uses the literal alias "alias" (getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)) instead of "idp-alias-20". Same failure mode as the loop cleanup: the second-created IDP is never removed, and the dangling cleanup resource hits a nonexistent alias, so any assertion about realm state after this test is polluted.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, both the loop creating `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19` and the later creation of `idp-alias-20` register cleanup with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`. This uses the literal string "alias" instead of the actual created alias (e.g., `idpRep.getAlias()` / `"idp-alias-20"`), so the created IDPs will not be removed and the cleanup may attempt to remove a non-existent IDP, polluting realm state for subsequent assertions/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test verifies only the cache's internal IdentityProviderListQuery contents (getIDPs sizes); it never asserts the Stream returned by getForLogin() itself in any scenario. The most important behavior — what callers actually receive — is unverified. Notably, the cached path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin returns models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping applied on the isInvalid path, so cached and uncached calls can return differently-shaped models; a content assertion on the returned stream would catch this, but the test passes either way because it never looks at the return value. Checked files: OrganizationCacheTest.java is the only test file in this diff touching getForLogin.

adjudication.rationale: In the added OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin(), the calls to session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) are never asserted for returned content/shape; the test only inspects the internal cache entry (IdentityProviderListQuery) and its getIDPs(...).size(). That is a concrete, diff-grounded gap because the new caching logic in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin has two paths (isInvalid() uses idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel), while the cached path returns identityProviders.stream() after loading by id). Even if the cached path might still return wrapped models via getById (not shown in this diff), the test as written would not detect any behavioral divergence in the returned Stream, only cache bookkeeping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new branch where a cache entry exists but getIDPs(searchKey) returns null (query present, new organizationId search) has no test triggering it — the test only ever calls getForLogin with the same organizationId (or null) used to populate the cache, and asserts counts, never the invalidateObject/re-add path with a second organization. The multi-organization merge path — invalidateObject, re-fetch, and the new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, ..., query) constructor that must carry over the previously cached search keys — is entirely unexercised; a regression that drops the prior searchKey's IDP set (e.g. showing an empty login page for the first org after a second org logs in) passes the suite. Checked files: only OrganizationCacheTest.java touches this provider, and it never calls getForLogin with a second, distinct organizationId.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nontrivial caching branch in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`: when a cache entry exists (`query != null`) but `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns `null`, it executes `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds the entry via `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` to merge/carry over previously cached search keys. The added `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` only calls `getForLogin` with `organizationId == null` and a single `orgaId`, so it never triggers the “query present, new searchKey not yet cached” path. This leaves the merge/carry-over behavior of the constructor overload unexercised, which is a concrete test gap tied directly to the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The stale-entry fallback branch (session.identityProviders().getById(id) == null → registerInvalidation and re-fetch from delegate) is never triggered by any test. This is the cache-poisoning recovery path — a cached IDP list referencing a since-deleted IDP (e.g. deleted by another node or a path that bypassed invalidation). If this branch has a bug (wrong key invalidated, or the delegate re-fetch also wrong), users get an empty or erroring login page permanently, and no test in the diff would notice. Checked files: OrganizationCacheTest.java never creates the condition of a cached list containing a nonexistent internalId.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new caching implementation for getForLogin() in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider, including a recovery branch: when iterating cached internalIds, if session.identityProviders().getById(id) returns null it calls realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey) and falls back to idpDelegate.getForLogin(...). In the added test testCacheIDPForLogin(), all manipulations (create/update/remove) occur through the normal APIs that also register invalidations, and the assertions only check presence/absence of cache entries and expected sizes after invalidations. The test never creates the specific condition where the cached IDP list contains an internalId that no longer exists (e.g., deletion bypassing invalidation / remote node), so this cache-poisoning recovery path is not exercised by any test shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) and that method dereferences original (original.getOrganizationId()) without a null check, so updating an IDP whose getById lookup returns null throws NullPointerException before the delegate update runs. Any update() where the underlying provider returns null for the internalId (e.g. custom IDP storage where cached lookup misses and delegate returns null, or stale internalId passed by a caller) crashes with NPE instead of updating, leaving the IDP unmodifiable and the login caches un-invalidated.

adjudication.rationale: The new `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` does not dereference `original` unconditionally. It calls `getLoginPredicate().test(original)`, and `getLoginPredicate()` (as shown in the diff) is explicitly guarded with `Objects::nonNull`, so `test(null)` is `false`. The only place `original.getOrganizationId()` is used is in an `&&` condition that is only evaluated when `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is `true`, which cannot happen for `null` due to the non-null guard (short-circuit prevents the dereference). Also, `update()` already called `registerIDPInvalidation(idpById)` before this change, so any null-handling issue around `idpById` is not introduced by the added login invalidation call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a cache entry exists but lacks the current organizationId searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) locally and then re-reads getCurrentRevision and replaces the query, so the invalidation is not propagated to other cluster nodes the way registerInvalidation-based invalidations are, while the new query is only addRevisioned on this node's current counter. In a multi-node cluster, node A caches the org-scoped list while node B retains the previous query object lacking that searchKey (or vice versa after revision races), so subsequent getForLogin calls on other nodes take the invalidate-and-replace path repeatedly, degrading to per-request cache misses or serving a query whose revision predates a concurrent update — stale login IDP lists shown on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin(...)` caching logic, when an existing `IdentityProviderListQuery` is present but does not contain the current `searchKey`, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey);` and then rebuilds/re-adds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` (`cache.addRevisioned(...)`). This differs from the rest of this class, which uses `realmCache.registerInvalidation(...)` to invalidate keys (e.g., `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). From the diff alone we can verify this inconsistency (invalidateObject vs registerInvalidation) and that it could matter in clustered setups where invalidations are expected to be propagated via the `registerInvalidation` mechanism. However, the diff does not define the cluster semantics of `invalidateObject`, so the claim that it is strictly “local” (and thus causes stale lists on other nodes) cannot be fully proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a cached internalId no longer resolves (getById returns null), the code registers invalidation of only the single cacheKey for the current (realm, mode) and falls back to the delegate, leaving the other FetchMode caches for the same realm populated with the same stale id set. After an IDP is removed in a way that bypassed this provider's invalidation hooks (e.g. direct persistence-layer delete or another node's race), every FetchMode cache (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) holds the dangling id; each mode's first access falls into the same fallback, and between invalidation and re-population users on the login page can be served lists from the still-stale sibling-mode caches.

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(...)`, when a cached internalId no longer resolves (`idp == null`), the code does `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey);` where `cacheKey` is only for the current `FetchMode` (`cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)`), then falls back to the delegate. The diff does not show any invalidation of the other mode keys for the same realm in this path, so sibling-mode caches can remain populated with the dangling id until they are accessed (at which point they’ll also invalidate themselves). However, the method will not serve a stale list to the caller in this situation because it returns the delegate result immediately upon encountering `null`, rather than returning the partially-built `identityProviders` set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate arm `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, unlike the existing filter chain which may tolerate config-less models. Any IdentityProviderModel returned by a custom storage or legacy data where getConfig() returns null now throws NPE from getLoginPredicate during every login-page IDP listing and during every create/update/remove through the Infinispan cache provider, breaking login flows for that realm until the row is fixed.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new arm to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
This unconditionally calls `idp.getConfig().get(...)` when `getOrganizationId() != null`. There is no null-guard around `idp.getConfig()`, so if any `IdentityProviderModel` implementation returns `null` for `getConfig()` (e.g., custom storage/legacy models), `getLoginPredicate()` will throw an NPE. Since the new Infinispan provider logic invokes `getLoginPredicate()` in `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` during create/update/remove, and `getForLogin(...)` is used for login-page listings, such an NPE would break those flows for affected realms/models.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and never applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cache hits and cache misses return differently-shaped IdentityProviderModel objects. The cache-miss/isInvalid branches wrap every delegate result with this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (organization-aware enable/disable semantics), but the cached branch returns raw models from getById. A user hitting the login page after the list query is cached gets unwrapped models, producing different visibility/enablement behavior than the first, uncached request — the exact class of bug the freemarker isEnabled re-check in this same diff papers over, meaning the cached path can list IDPs on the login page that the uncached path would have hidden.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path (`isInvalid(cacheKey)` and the fallback when an IDP is null) returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, explicitly wrapping models. But on the cache-hit path it reconstructs results by iterating cached internal IDs and doing `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and then returns `identityProviders.stream()` with no call to `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, that means cached vs uncached executions can return different model instances (wrapped vs not), matching the concern about inconsistent enable/visibility behavior (also hinted by the added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check comment in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate clause dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, so any IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set but a null config map throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate. getLoginPredicate().test(idp) is now invoked from InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/remove/update invalidation paths (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), so creating or updating an organization-linked IDP whose config map is null (models constructed programmatically or by storage providers that leave config unset) throws NPE and aborts the admin write operation instead of just skipping cache invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` the clause `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. For any `IdentityProviderModel` with a non-null `organizationId`, this will evaluate `idp.getConfig().get(...)` without guarding `getConfig()` against null, which would throw an NPE if the config map is null. The diff also introduces new call sites of `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` in admin write paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation` on create/remove and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` on update), so such an NPE would abort those operations rather than merely skipping invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove(String alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a delegate/DB hit) even on the branch where isInvalid(cacheKey) is true and the result is only used for invalidation bookkeeping. Every IDP removal in a realm using the infinispan cache pays an extra storage lookup on the hot admin path even when the login-cache invalidation it feeds will be a no-op for a non-login IDP; operators of large realms see doubled read load on IDP removal with no correctness benefit when the IDP does not qualify for login.

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff introduces an unconditional delegate lookup: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. Previously, `getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path (and otherwise the cached entry was used). The new unconditional call is then used for `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` (in the invalid branch) and for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` after `registerCountInvalidation()`. This is a diff-grounded performance/load concern (extra storage/DB hit on every removal) rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getForLogin cache stores per-organizationId sets inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode and, on a miss for a new searchKey, invalidates the whole object and re-adds with cache.getCurrentCounter(), a different revision basis than the startupRevision used on the first populate. When addRevisioned in the second branch fails because the revision/counter basis is not newer than the entry concurrently re-populated by another node (the two populate paths use inconsistent revision sources: startupRevision vs getCurrentCounter), the freshly loaded set for the new organizationId is silently discarded — every login-page request for that organization keeps missing the cache and re-hits the delegate storage, turning the login cache into a permanent passthrough for that org with no error or metric surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin()` cache implementation, the initial population path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)` when `query == null`, but the “new searchKey” path (when `cached == null`) invalidates and then uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This inconsistency in the revision/counter source is directly visible in the diff and can create a concurrency/ordering risk in revisioned-cache semantics. However, the finding’s stronger claim (that `addRevisioned` can fail silently, causing a permanent passthrough for that org) is not verifiable from the diff because the behavior of `addRevisioned` on revision conflicts isn’t shown here.
